title: Priority-lease routing: windowed guarantees with opportunistic spillover
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Free/paid/enterprise lanes often have competing short-term demand spikes. Current admission controllers either strictly enforce plan quotas (causing high latency/denials during bursts) or aggressively demote traffic (hurting enterprise SLAs). We need a lightweight routing primitive that can give short-duration, soft guarantees to higher-tier traffic while allowing unused capacity to be opportunistically consumed by lower tiers with fast eviction and accounting.
proposal_summary: Introduce a priority-lease abstraction: when a request is admitted into a reserved lane it consumes a short-lived lease token (lease duration configurable per plan). Leases provide a windowed soft guarantee (e.g., 5s) where the holder is prioritized for scheduling. If capacity tightens, leases are revoked in LRU or priority order with an eviction grace. Unused or expired leases free capacity for lower tiers. Lower-tier requests may consume leftover capacity via opportunistic spot lanes subject to preemption. System tracks lease issuance and revocation for accounting and quota reconciliation.
design_notes: Lease token lifecycle: issue -> active -> revoked/expired -> settle
Configurable parameters per plan: lease_duration_seconds, max_concurrent_leases, eviction_policy (LRU | oldest-first | credit-score)
Admission path integrates with existing global admission controller; leases are thin metadata attached to request context and stored in a small sharded in-memory store on each routing tier
Fallback behavior: on eviction, request either retries to spot lane (with backoff) or falls back to a compatible lower-capacity model variant (configured per plan)
Accounting: every lease issue/revoke emits events to console metrics and billing pipeline for per-tenant reconciliation
acceptance_criteria: Higher-tier (enterprise) p95 latency under burst preserved within 1.2x baseline for 90% of tenant bursts in synthetic tests
Free-tier best-effort throughput improves for low-utilization windows by at least 8% due to opportunistic spillover
No regressions in cold-start eviction rates and no increase in error-rate >0.5% on routes using leases
End-to-end telemetry (lease_issued, lease_revoked, lease_expired) visible in Console dashboards and correlates with routing decisions

E2E: create synthetic burst harness for free/paid/enterprise scenarios (owner: Li Chen)
Integrations: hook lease events into Console metrics and billing stream (owner: Priya Rao)
Safety: run chaos experiments to validate eviction grace and no deadlocks (owner: SRE team)

rollout_plan: Gate behind feature flag 'priority_lease_v1'. Deploy implementation to canary region (us-west-2) with 10% of enterprise traffic. Monitor lease metrics and p95 latency for 24h. If stable, expand to remaining regions in two waves: 50% then 100%. Enable opportunistic spot lanes for free-tier only after first full-region rollout. If any regression >SLO thresholds, flip flag off and rollback to previous admission controller.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Lease state divergence across routing nodes leading to double-counting. Mitigation: keep leases locally authoritative per shard and add monotonic lease IDs plus periodic reconciliation to central audit log.
Risk: High churn of short leases creates CPU overhead. Mitigation: cap max_concurrent_leases per shard and use batching for revocation notifications.

Risk: Unexpected billing deltas from frequent preemption. Mitigation: emit detailed lease events and run reconciliation job prior to billing cycle; cap preemptions logged to customers via usage report.
Risk: Tenant unhappy with frequent demotions. Mitigation: expose tenant-level telemetry and allow per-tenant lease tuning for enterprise customers under support agreement.
open_questions: Q1: Optimal default lease duration for text-generation workloads with 200-500ms token latencies? (suggestions: 3s, 5s, 10s)
Q2: Should leases be transferrable between regional pools during regional failover? If yes, how to keep eviction order consistent?
Q3: Billing model for opportunistic usage: credit vs zero-charge best-effort? Need PM guidance
decisions: Decided to start with 5s default lease window and make it configurable per plan
Use LRU eviction for initial rollout; allow switch to credit-score policy after metrics collection
Leases will not be globally transferable in v1 — regional shards authoritative
